meta.verificationNote: Every factual claim on this site is sourced. Primary sources are FUFA publications (club licensing decisions, the Article 13 ownership register, licensing timelines), published match reports and the club's own channels. cupTies.tie: Kumi United FC vs CATDA FC
cupTies.story: Drawn away to Kumi United in the Round of 64 of the Stanbic Uganda Cup. The result is not captured in the sources reviewed and will be added from the FUFA record.

Drawn against the defending champions. CATDA, then a third-tier side, held Kitara goalless for 71 minutes before Patrick Kaddu scored. CATDA equalised in the 84th minute. An own goal by Martin Kikambwe three minutes later settled the tie. The holders needed an own goal to get past the Lufula Boys.

The tie that made the name. John Revita and Moses Aliro scored as the Ugandan champions laboured to a two-goal win. Afterwards KCCA manager Mike Mutebi, the most decorated coach in the country's modern era, gave CATDA the endorsement no grassroots club in Uganda can buy.

quote.text: They asked a lot of questions and we almost answered. It is the best side we have played against this season. They were threatening in every department.

timeline.detail: CATDA win the Nakawa District League and are promoted into the Kampala Regional League, the third tier of Ugandan football.
A second-placed finish in a first Kampala Regional League season marks the club out as promotion contenders. The club is registered under the Kampala FA and playing out of Industrial Area.

timeline.event: The best side we have played, says KCCA
timeline.detail: In the Stanbic Uganda Cup Round of 64, a third-tier CATDA take the Ugandan champions to the limit before losing 2-0. Mike Mutebi's verdict puts the club on the national map.

timeline.event: One match from the Big League
timeline.detail: CATDA win the Kampala regional play-off 2-0 against Edgars at the FUFA Technical Centre in Njeru, missing three players and head coach Richard Amatre to positive COVID-19 tests, then lose the inter-regional final to Buganda champions Luweero United.

timeline.event: Top of the Scorpion Group, then penalties
timeline.detail: CATDA top the KRL Scorpion Group with 54 points from 21 games. Hudson Mbalire scores 19. In the play-off final at Muteesa II Stadium they draw 1-1 with Proline and lose 6-7 on spot kicks.
Drawn against defending Stanbic Uganda Cup champions Kitara in the Round of 32, CATDA keep them scoreless for 71 minutes and equalise in the 84th before an own goal decides it 2-1.

timeline.event: Champions of Kampala, promoted to the FUFA Big League
timeline.detail: In heavy rain at MTN Omondi Stadium, Lugogo, CATDA beat Ntinda United 4-2 on penalties after 0-0 to win the Kampala region and take the tier-two place. Michael Abura is named play-off MVP.

timeline.event: Licensed by FUFA for the Big League
timeline.detail: The FUFA Club Licensing Committee names CATDA FC among the 14 clubs granted a licence for the 2025/26 FUFA Big League. Bugolobi Coffee Grounds passes at the second stadium inspection.

timeline.event: First season in the FUFA Big League
timeline.detail: Nine wins, ten draws, eleven defeats. 37 points and 10th of 16, three clear of the relegation places. Survival secured in a national 16-club division.
CATDA close their debut Big League campaign by beating promotion-chasing Kigezi Home Boyz 1-0 at the Al Madina Stadium in Kabale.
The 2026/27 FUFA Big League kicks off. CATDA return as an established national second-tier club.

community.intro: CATDA are owned by their community in the literal, legal sense. The FUFA ownership register records the City Abattoir Traders Development Association as the largest single subscriber at 35%, alongside six natural persons from the same community. No corporation, ministry or external investor holds a share.

pillars.title: Community ownership
pillars.body: The traders' association holds 35% and six individuals from the abattoir community hold the balance, per the FUFA register for 2025/26. Funding follows the same structure: contributions from inside the trading community rather than a single external owner.

pillars.title: Youth pathway
pillars.body: The squad is built from Kampala neighbourhood networks, teenagers and players in their early twenties. Sharif "Diao" Ssengendo is the proof of concept: a CATDA goalscorer in the Kampala Regional League who went on to play in the Uganda Premier League with KCCA FC.

pillars.title: Governance
pillars.body: CATDA submit to the full FUFA club licensing cycle every season: ownership declarations under Article 13, licensing documents, stadium inspections and player registration minimums. They have also taken part in FUFA Clubs Pro-Agenda governance engagement run through the Kampala Regional FA.

pillars.title: Facilities
pillars.body: The club owns no stadium. Home is the Bugolobi Coffee Grounds, which passed FUFA stadium classification at the second inspection in August 2025. Cup ties and play-off finals have been staged at Kakungulu Memorial School grounds, MTN Omondi Stadium, Muteesa II Stadium and the FUFA Technical Centre.

needs: Floodlighting and stand improvements at Bugolobi Coffee Grounds to hold FUFA stadium classification each season
A squad retention fund to compete with Uganda Premier League wages for players the club developed
An away-travel budget for a national 16-club division spanning Kabale, Kumi, Mbale, Arua and Nebbi
A formal youth academy structure below the first team in Nakawa and Industrial Area
Commercial partners who want grassroots credibility and a documented national story

pillars.title: The climb
pillars.body: Nakawa District champions in 2017/18. Seven seasons in the Kampala Regional League. Two play-off final defeats, one on penalties and one by a single goal in an inter-regional decider. Then champions of the Kampala region in May 2025, a FUFA licence in August 2025, and a national second-tier place held ever since.

pillars.title: The giant killers
pillars.body: Ugandan champions KCCA needed 90 hard minutes in the 2021 Uganda Cup and afterwards called CATDA the best side they had faced all season. Defending cup holders Kitara needed an own goal in the 87th minute to escape in 2025. Nobody draws CATDA in the cup and relaxes.

pillars.title: The Lufula
pillars.body: The club belongs to the abattoir community on Old Port Bell Road. Traders, butchers and workers fund it, own it and fill the touchline with drums. The crest says it plainly: Kick With Skills, Lufula.

news.title: Season two: CATDA FC return to the FUFA Big League
news.body: The 2026/27 FUFA Big League kicks off on Sunday 27 September 2026, after FUFA released the first-round fixtures on 15 September 2026. CATDA return as an established national second-tier club after finishing 10th of 16 in their debut campaign with 37 points, three clear of the relegation places. Opening fixture details will be published here once confirmed by the club.

news.title: Kigezi Home Boyz 0-1 CATDA: a final-day statement in Kabale
news.body: CATDA ended their first season in the FUFA Big League by travelling to the Al Madina Stadium in Kabale and beating a Kigezi Home Boyz side chasing promotion. The result confirmed survival with a win and sent the Lufula Boys into the off-season unbeaten in their last three recorded fixtures.

news.title: CATDA 2-1 Ntugasaze: three points at Bugolobi
news.body: Ntugasaze finished second in the division and were promoted to the StarTimes Uganda Premier League. CATDA beat them at the Bugolobi Coffee Grounds on match day 23.

news.title: Champions of Kampala, promoted to the FUFA Big League
news.body: In pouring rain at MTN Omondi Stadium, Lugogo, CATDA and Ntinda United played out a goalless 90 minutes in the 2024/25 Kampala region play-off final. On penalties CATDA won 4-2 and took the Kampala region's place in the FUFA Big League for 2025/26. Michael Abura was named Most Valuable Player of the play-offs.
